title: Only one branch runs
idea: Tracing if/else: the condition picks exactly one branch. The other is always skipped. Careful tracing, thinking-heavy.

exercises.explanation: 70 >= 50 is True, so only the if branch runs: Pass.
30 >= 50 is False, so only the else branch runs: Fail.

exercises.prompt: In an if/else, both branches can run at the same time.
exercises.explanation: No - exactly one branch runs. The condition chooses; the other branch is skipped.
5 == 5 is True, so only 'five' prints. Exactly one line.
8 % 2 is 0, and 0 == 0 is True, so the if branch runs: even.
7 % 2 is 1, and 1 == 0 is False, so the else branch runs: odd.
n > 0 is True only for 5 here. 0 and -3 fall to the else branch.

exercises.prompt: If the if branch runs, the else branch is skipped.
exercises.explanation: Yes - they are the two halves of one choice. Only the chosen half runs.

exercises.prompt:
What prints after the whole thing?

n = 4
if n > 10:
    print("big")
else:
    print("small")
print("done")
exercises.explanation: n > 10 is False so else runs ('small'). Then the unindented 'done' always runs after the choice.

exercises.prompt: Why is it reassuring that exactly one branch always runs?
options: Every case is covered - no situation is left without an outcome
exercises.explanation: if/else guarantees an outcome for both True and False - nothing slips through unhandled.
